newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zaire's Tutsi rebels plan new refugee corridor-UN.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Tutsi rebels plan new refugee corridor-UN.

text.p: Tutsi rebels controlling eastern Zaire have told U.N. officials that they plan to open a return corridor in Bukavu region for tens of thousands of scattered Hutu refugees, the U.N. refugee agency said on Monday.

UNHCR spokesman Fernando Del Mundo told Reuters that the new authorities in eastern Zaire told U.N. agencies that the corridor from Bukavu south of Lake Kivu to Rwanda's southwestern Cyangugu border crossing could be opened on Tuesday.

He said UNHCR had no details of the planned corridor, which suggests that Tutsi rebels see signs of possible movement from Bukavu following a weekend exodus into Rwanda from Goma further to the north after they dispersed extremists with shelling.
More than 500,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees returned home from Goma at the weekend after Tutsi rebels shelled Mugunga camp and forced extremist Hutu militiamen to flee to the hills.

Aid agencies have pulled out of Bukavu because of insecurity and Del Mundo said UNHCR had no reports of any movement by some 500,000 refugees in the region. Aid sources in Geneva said some refugees from Bukavu area were moving north towards Goma.
"The refugees are spread out all over the place. We don't know ehere they are," he said.

An International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) spokesman said on Monday that a Zairean Red Cross worker who had walked 350 km (220 miles) in 17 days from the rebel-held town of Bukavu had reported seeing thousands of people all along the way.
